paragraphs.text: Second-hand clothing was once associated mainly with people who could not afford anything else. That image has changed, and I think the change is long overdue.

The environmental case is strong. Producing new clothes uses large amounts of water and energy, and many garments are worn only a few times before being thrown away. Buying used clothes extends their life and reduces the demand for new ones.
Some people object that second-hand clothes are unhygienic. In my view this concern is exaggerated: most charity shops check items before selling them, and a normal wash is all that is needed.

I would not claim that second-hand shopping suits everyone. Finding the right size can take time, and people who need special clothing for work may have little choice. But for everyday items, it is worth trying before buying new.
Swapping clothes with friends is another option I would encourage. Several community groups in my area hold swap events each season, and the only cost is the time it takes to look through the rails.

items.prompt: The writer welcomes the change in attitudes to second-hand clothes.
The writer thinks the environmental argument for second-hand clothes is weak.
The writer agrees that second-hand clothes are a serious health risk.
The writer thinks charity shops charge too much for their clothes.
The writer recommends trying second-hand clothes for everyday items.
